##

### use Mock Service Worker

[quick start guide] (https://mswjs.io/docs/quick-start/)

✅ a. Using msw (Mock Service Worker) – THE BEST way

```ts
npm install msw --save-dev
```


📁 Folder Structure (recommended)
```ts
src/
  mocks/
    handlers.ts
    browser.ts
  index.tsx

```

Defines a list of mock API endpoints and how to respond to them.

```ts
// src/mocks/handlers.ts
import { rest } from 'msw'

export const handlers = [
  rest.get('/api/user', (req, res, ctx) => {
    return res(ctx.status(200), ctx.json({ id: 1, name: 'Amit Verma' }))
  }),

  rest.post('/api/login', (req, res, ctx) => {
    return res(ctx.status(200), ctx.json({ token: 'abc123' }))
  }),
]
```


📌 Sets up the MSW worker in the browser and uses the handlers from handlers.ts.

```ts
// src/mocks/browser.ts
import { setupWorker } from 'msw'
import { handlers } from './handlers'

export const worker = setupWorker(...handlers)
```

🧠 This acts like your mock backend — it returns fake data instead of calling the real server.


Then in index.tsx:

```ts
if (process.env.NODE_ENV === 'development') {
  const { worker } = await import('./mocks/browser')
  worker.start()
}
```

setupWorker() starts a Service Worker that listens to fetch and intercepts API calls in the browser.


🔄 Flow Summary
```js
App → fetch('/api/user')
     ↓
[MSW Service Worker]
     ↓
handlers.ts → Matches rest.get('/api/user')
     ↓
Returns mocked response (e.g. { id: 1, name: "Amit" })
```

🧪 Test It

In your React component, write:

```ts
useEffect(() => {
  fetch('/api/user')
    .then(res => res.json())
    .then(data => console.log('Mocked User:', data))
}, [])
```

When you run your app, it should log:
Mocked User: { id: 1, name: 'Amit Verma', role: 'Lead Software Engineer' }
